name: Comms Array
narrativeOnEnter: A tight room — just equipment racks, a transmitter console, and a satellite dish control terminal. The distress beacon is blinking orange: active, but unconfirmed. A cabinet on the wall has an external airlock indicator behind a cracked glass panel.

hotspots.label: External Airlock
hotspots.lockedMessage: External airlock is in emergency lockdown — reactor instability prevents safe EVA. Stabilise the reactor first.

action.text:
MERIDIAN STATION — DISTRESS BEACON PROTOCOL

Beacon is active. Rescue shuttle is in position.
To confirm evacuation and authorise approach:

1. Stabilise reactor (required for safe beacon confirmation)
2. Access the escape pod bay for passenger manifest upload
3. OR: use external airlock EVA route to dock directly
   (EVA route requires reactor stabilisation — no active radiation fields)

Emergency beacon transmission will automatically signal shuttle
upon reactor stabilisation completion.

───
Kovalev's handwriting, on a note tucked inside the manual:

'Do not let the beacon auto-signal MERIDIAN-3.
Override the auto-signal before reactor sequence completes.
Manually transmit on 148.350 MHz instead.

MERIDIAN-3 will tell you they're from HELIOS GROUP.
HELIOS GROUP is AXIOM. Their shuttle carries a portable SRR extraction unit.
If they dock, they will board with a team and attempt to pull the buffer data
before the thermal wipe completes.
Do not give them that window.

CALLISTO is the real rescue.
They are a whistleblower network — IREX Board — operating outside AXIOM channels.
They have testimony from Dr. Elara Voss, who survived Blackwood.
They have Kira Reiss's server logs from Arcadia.
They know what PROMETHEUS is.
And they know what AXIOM will do if they get six more neural maps to build the next one.

Transmit: "Buffer is clean. Kovalev's message."
They will know what it means. They will come in.
— D.K.'

The transmitter console shows two active signals.

SIGNAL 1 — Standard emergency frequency:
SHUTTLE MERIDIAN-3 RESPONSE:
'Station acknowledged. Holding position. Awaiting confirmation of crew manifest and reactor status before approach. Sending response to EVA channel: airlock accessible from Comms Array once radiation clear.'

SIGNAL 2 — 148.350 MHz (encrypted burst, partially decoded):
HEADER: CALLISTO / IREX BOARD — INDEPENDENT RESEARCH ETHICS EXCHANGE

'MERIDIAN STATION — WE KNOW ABOUT HELIOS.
WE HAVE THE BLACKWOOD FILES.
WE HAVE TESTIMONY FROM DR. ELARA VOSS AND K. REISS.
WE HAVE THE ARCADIA SERVER LOGS.

KOVALEV — IF YOU ARE READING THIS — WE ARE AT 148.350.
DO NOT BOARD MERIDIAN-3.
REPEAT: DO NOT BOARD MERIDIAN-3.
THEY WILL TELL YOU THEY ARE RESCUE.
THEY ARE EXTRACTION.

WHEN THE REACTOR IS STABLE: TRANSMIT ON THIS FREQUENCY.
WE WILL COME IN.'

───
A second burst, timestamp 03:41 — the moment Arcadia's network went dark. Origin: unknown. Signal pattern matches no registered vessel or station.

'I HAVE THE NAMES.
ALL 47.
AND NOW ALL 6.
TELL CALLISTO: THE DATA MUST NOT REACH AXIOM.
I HAVE BEEN WAITING FIFTEEN YEARS TO SAY THIS.
— P'

EXTERNAL AIRLOCK — EVA STATUS

Status: LOCKED (Reactor radiation field active)
Clearance required: Reactor deck — NOMINAL status

Once reactor is stabilised, this airlock will automatically unlock.
Distance to rescue shuttle: 40 metres. EVA tether required.
